Elastic Cache Walkthrough

Designing a 1B-key product cache that scales 10 → 50 nodes on a weighted vnode ring - requirements, numbers, components.

RequirementsMovement mathRing metadataRouting SDK

Quick Revision

  • Canonical product key → client SDK → versioned weighted vnode ring.
  • Primary + cross-zone replicas; single-flight DB fallback.
  • Controlled join/drain; redirect on stale epoch.
  • 10 → 11 nodes moves ~91 GB, not ~909 GB.
  • Hot keys monitored and mitigated separately.

Requirements → decisions

AskAnswerDecision
Authoritative?No, DB is truthLost entries refill; protect origin
Why not modulo?Autoscaling, failuresRing or logical slots
Node count?10 now, 10-50 in 2 yearsVersioned metadata, automatic join/removal
Data?1B keys, ~1 KBMeasure movement in bytes
Change frequency?Weekly planned, rare failuresSafe controlled moves
Identical nodes?Some 2× memoryWeighted ownership
Traffic?Flash sale 100K QPSNear cache, replicas, single-flight, limits

Consistency?Brief staleness OKReplica reads allowed

Stale metadata?PossibleEpoch + redirect + bounded retry
Multi-key?Some product subkeysShared routing key / hash tag
Temporary failure?Prefer replica fallbackSuspicion window, anti-flap

Estimation

1B keys × 1 KB ≈ 1 TB logical; RF 3 ≈ 3 TB physical
10 → 11 nodes: modulo ≈ 909 GB moved · ring ≈ 91 GB moved
removing a node: ≈ total / N reassigned
weighted: expected_bytes_i = logical × weight_i / Σ weights
metadata: 50 nodes × 256 vnodes × 128 B ≈ 1.64 MB
migration: 180 GB / 100 MB/s ≈ 30 min (+ catch-up, validation, rollback)
hot key: 100K QPS / 20K per node → 5 copies

Components and metadata

  • Clients - issue reads/writes.
  • Routing SDK - canonicalize, hash, search tokens, choose primary/replicas, cache membership.
  • Membership service - node IDs, tokens, weights, state, zones, epoch.
  • Cache nodes - own token ranges.
  • Failure detector - reports health; doesn't delete ownership on its own.
  • Rebalance controller - plans moves, throttles, validates, publishes epochs.
  • Origin DB - source of truth. Metrics/audit - ownership, traffic, redirects, movement.

Interview practice

Answer aloud, then reveal.

When pick fixed slots over a ring?

When enumerable migration units and simple operational control matter more than continuous token distribution.

What metrics prove the ring is healthy?

Per-node keys, bytes, QPS, p99, resources; hot-key concentration; replica placement; redirects; epochs; bytes moved; lag; validation errors; origin fallback QPS.

Strongest senior-level takeaway?

Consistent hashing is only the placement primitive; the full design adds membership consensus, versioning, topology-aware replication, failure policy, migration, validation, rollback, hot-key handling, and observability.
